tasks.short: Prepare forestry syllabi, assignments and handouts

steps.what: Define learning outcomes, assessment purpose and course material requirements
Gather current forestry sources and existing course materials
Draft syllabi, homework assignments and handout content

loop.purpose: Draft source-grounded material matching course objectives
loop.output: Draft syllabus, assignments or handouts with references
loop.check: The teacher checks factual meaning, learning alignment, assignment solvability and every reference against the source material.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims or unsound assignments return to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Reuse and formatting are native; new explanations and assignment wording require context-specific drafting.

steps.what: Check materials for accuracy, workload, accessibility and assessment alignment
Format checked course content into the required material layouts

tasks.design: Use native {DOCS} layouts and {LMS} source views, with a bounded drafting loop for new course text. The teacher retains learning design and content checks; deterministic formatting prepares the materials without publishing them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source gathering, restatement and layout can repeat across course documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit objectives and source packets support checked drafts, while native layouts handle formatting.
tasks.still_hard: An attractive assignment can still teach or assess the wrong thing.
tasks.human_edge: Choose meaningful objectives and judge whether the task is educationally sound.
tasks.altitude: Spend material preparation on educational quality and checked content.

evidence.claim: Source-grounded drafting and native layouts could reduce repeated material preparation; the saving is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: The task prepares the requested materials. No extra publication, approval meeting or activity log is assumed; ordinary author saves remain retained within writing/checking time.

The teacher produces objectives, student level, schedule and assignment purpose in s1 and selects source versions in s2. Retained time includes capturing and checking these inputs; missing sources stop affected drafting for manual preparation.
Native source views remove 3 hours of navigation only. S5 removes real layout work, not a same-system save. Existing course material is reused before drafting new text.
Lecture-specific preparation overlapping task 5824 is counted once per actual material.
unknowns: How much current text and formatting are already reusable.
research_questions: Compare full preparation and correction time for syllabi, assignments and handouts, including assignment solvability.

already_counted.description: Review draft material and check educational quality

incremental.description: Maintain source checks and material layouts

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=67, gross 33 minus 3 upkeep gives central net 30. Conservative case: weak source indexing retains 14/15 source hours, new pedagogy retains 36/40 drafting hours and layout incompatibility retains 7/10 formatting hours plus 35 fixed: 92 retained, 8 gross minus 3 =5. Suitable sources and compatible layouts retain 13 source, 25 drafting and 3 formatting hours plus 35 fixed: 76 retained, 24 gross minus 3 =21.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Choose lecture objectives and sequence for the student group
Select current forest policy, pathology or mapping sources
Write lecture explanations, examples and speaking material

loop.purpose: Draft explanations for the selected forestry lecture
loop.check: The teacher checks factual meaning, example validity and suitability for the students against the source material.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims or unsuitable examples return to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Existing lectures are reused first; context-specific explanations require language beyond fixed layouts.

steps.what: Check the lecture content and examples before teaching
Format the checked lecture material using its existing layout
Deliver lectures and respond to undergraduate or graduate students

tasks.design: Prepare source-grounded lecture text in {DOCS} with a bounded drafting loop and native formatting. The teacher retains lecture design, checking and delivery, including a check of the formatted material used with students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rewording existing evidence and arranging lecture material can repeat preparation work.
tasks.enabler_now: Selected source packets and native layouts support checked drafting and formatting.
tasks.still_hard: The teacher must respond to students' understanding and connect concepts to practice.
tasks.human_edge: Explain and adapt during live teaching.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated lecture preparation while retaining teaching responsibility.

reach.learn: Keep examples connected to current evidence.

evidence.claim: Checked lecture drafting and native formatting could reduce repeated preparation; delivery and time estimates remain unmeasured.

assumptions: The boundary includes preparation and delivery. Course material shared with task 5829 is counted once in an actual course, not added twice.
The teacher produces objectives and sequence in s1 and selected source versions in s2; all capture and relevance checking remains. Missing evidence returns the relevant section to manual preparation.
The native source view removes only 1 hour of repeated navigation; s5 removes actual layout work. Reuse current lectures before new drafting, and count no existing software runtime as labour saving.
No grading, publication or trailing lecture log is added. Ordinary saves stay retained without self-approval.
unknowns: How much existing lecture material can already be reused.
research_questions: Measure preparation and correction time across lectures with different levels of new content.

already_counted.description: Check lecture content and deliver teaching

incremental.description: Maintain lecture drafting checks and layouts

approvals.approved_version: Exact formatted lecture material and claims delivered to the current students; changed content requires checking again before presentation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=85, gross 15 minus 3 upkeep gives central net 12. Conservative case: limited source metadata retain all 10 source hours, difficult explanations retain 23/25 drafting hours and layout mismatch retains 3/5 formatting hours plus 60 fixed: 96 retained, 4 gross minus 3 =1. Suitable sources and layouts retain 9 source, 19 drafting and 2 formatting hours plus 60 fixed: 90 retained, 10 gross minus 3 =7.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate and grade student work and prepare feedback

steps.what: Gather students' class work, assignments and papers for marking
Review assignment criteria and the applicable grading rubric
Read the student work and identify relevant evidence
Evaluate the evidence and decide each student's grade
Write feedback explaining the marker's observations and grade

loop.purpose: Phrase feedback from the teacher's already decided observations
loop.input: Teacher's evidence notes, feedback points and rubric
loop.output: Draft feedback explaining those points without changing the grade
loop.check: The teacher checks every feedback statement against the student's work and her own decision, including tone and requested improvements.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported criticism or changed grading rationale returns to manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Native comment banks are used first; individual explanations require context-specific wording.

steps.what: Enter the decided grades in existing student grade fields
Release checked grades and feedback to the intended students

tasks.design: Configure native {LMS} submission views and student-linked grade fields, with a bounded feedback-writing loop based on the teacher's own marking notes. The teacher reads and evaluates all work, decides grades and controls the exact release to students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Submission navigation and feedback wording can consume time beside substantive marking.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing student identifiers and teacher notes support limited entry reuse and checked feedback drafting.
tasks.still_hard: A grade must reflect the student's actual evidence against the rubric.
tasks.human_edge: Judge understanding and give appropriate, defensible feedback.
tasks.altitude: Reduce clerical marking work while retaining examiner judgement.

reach.learn: Separate feedback wording from grade decisions.

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts feedback from instructor notes; this supports wording assistance rather than automatic grade decisions or measured savings.
The digest identifies Dutch examiner responsibilities under the WHW; this design retains grade decisions with the teacher in the authorised examiner role.

assumptions: The boundary includes evaluation, feedback writing, actual grade entry and release. It adds no separate marking activity log or invented second-system grade transfer.

Students produce submissions with identifiers in the current LMS process. Course owners maintain criteria and rubrics. The teacher produces evidence notes in s3 and decided grades/feedback points in s4, with all reading and decision time retained; missing identity or evidence returns to manual investigation.

Submission views remove 3 navigation hours. Student-linked fields remove 1 hour of repeated identifiers from grade entry, retaining the grade itself and ordinary save time; existing automatic identity linking has no benefit.
Use native comment banks before a model loop. No automatic scoring, student ranking or fraud detection is proposed.
unknowns: Whether policy permits feedback drafting with the current student data.
Whether identity fields and comment banks already remove this clerical work.
research_questions: Measure complete marking and feedback checking time while checking that generated feedback preserves the teacher's actual rationale.

incremental.description: Maintain feedback checks and student-linked entry settings

approvals.approved_version: Exact grades, feedback text, submission identifiers and student recipients; any changed result or recipient requires checking again before release.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=88, gross 12 minus 3 upkeep gives central net 9. Conservative case: mixed submission formats retain 9/10 intake hours, individual feedback needs retain 18/20 writing hours and unlinked identities retain all 5 entry hours plus 65 fixed: 97 retained, 3 gross minus 3 =0. Compatible identifiers and suitable teacher notes retain 8 intake, 15 feedback and 4 entry hours plus 65 fixed: 92 retained, 8 gross minus 3 =5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise students' laboratory and field work

steps.what: Review the current laboratory or field activity and student needs
Brief students on the activity, methods and immediate constraints
Observe students' laboratory or field work and assess their methods
Guide students and intervene when their methods or conditions require it

tasks.design: Retain direct supervision, using existing {DOCS} activity instructions and {LMS} context. Native views can support access, but no demonstrated supervision step loses time in this design.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supervision depends on the student's live method and the actual laboratory or field conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported digital substitution removes the teacher's observation and intervention time here.
tasks.still_hard: Conditions and students' actions can change during the activity.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise a learning or practical problem and intervene appropriately.

reach.learn: Observe the actual method before deciding what help is needed.

evidence.claim: Live practical supervision remains human in this design; there is no measured basis for removing observation or intervention time.

assumptions: The boundary includes current instruction review, briefing, observation and intervention. The statement establishes no separate supervision log, so no unused trailing record is added. Course-material creation and grading are separately represented by tasks 5829 and 5825 and counted once if shared.

Current activity owners supply instructions and site/laboratory information. The teacher checks these and student needs in s1, fully retaining capture and reading time; missing information requires direct clarification.
Native document and course views are already available support and do not remove a priced action here. No structured safety flag, attendance capture, automatic alert or student score is assumed.
Communication gates are immediate checks of the actual briefing or guidance, not new approval meetings. No new system means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Whether the institution has any separate current supervision record duty.
research_questions: Observe actual supervision and identify any existing lookup or record work before pricing a digital change.

already_counted.description: Observe practical work and guide students

incremental.description: No new system or maintenance work is introduced

approvals.approved_version: Actual activity briefing and constraints delivered to the current students; changed instructions require checking before delivery.
Actual guidance or intervention for the observed student method and conditions; changed advice is checked immediately before delivery.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=100, no incremental upkeep. All current review, briefing, observation and intervention remains. Native access support removes no demonstrated action, and no new record-writing baseline is invented; both cases retain the full task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Preserve teaching, examiner judgement and practical supervision while reducing specific material preparation and feedback wording.
reach: Compare assessment and practical teaching support with instructional coordinators and laboratory teaching staff.
role.ambitious_version: Forestry teaching supported by useful checked materials while teachers remain accountable for learning, assessment and practical guidance.

job.title: Forestry and Conservation Science Teachers, Postsecondary
